messages:
rachel.sre: Quick postmortem summary: during last night's release we saw a ~3.5x spike in gen-api cold-start P95 for a small subset of routes (primarily high-fanout webhook flows). Root cause: new routing change increased fanout for a cached prefix which exhausted per-shard hotset limits and triggered cascading evictions.

mika.prod: thanks for the summary. Are we planning any immediate policy changes?

rachel.sre: Yes  two actions: 1) emergency mitigation today: enable automatic model-degrade policy for affected routes to reduce tail latency (fallback to compact variant on sustained cold-path misses), 2) scheduled maintenance next Tue to increase per-shard hotset caps and add a slow-drain eviction throttle. Both will be rolled out with canaries.

jon.oncall: Whats the customer impact for the emergency mitigation?

rachel.sre: Very low: fallback to compact model adds ~6-8% cost savings per token and reduces P95 by ~300-450ms for affected requests. It may slightly change output quality; we'll only enable for routes that are non-critical (no compliance constraints). If teams prefer opt-out we can exclude them.

bench-bot: Perf note: compact variant tested on staging showed median latency down 220ms and P95 down 380ms under identical cache-miss workload.

deploy-bot: scheduling emergency job: job_id=emergency-fallback-2015556789, canary=4%

ops-bot: automated guardrails: will auto-abort if error-rate increases >0.4% absolute OR model-fallback-count >300/min sustained 5m OR P95 for non-fallback routes increases >250ms for 10m.

mika.prod: rollout plan details?

rachel.sre: Plan for emergency fallback today (window 02:15-02:45 UTC):
1) preflight: enable fallback flag on config for a 4% canary traffic group for 10m
2) if stable -> ramp to 25% for 15m with 5m observation windows
3) full enable within region over 30m if metrics normal
Abort if guards hit. Runbook commands:
```
# enable fallback for route group
curl -X POST https://internal-config/route-fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route_group":"webhook-highfanout","enable":true,"mode":"canary","percent":4}'
# rollback
curl -X POST https://internal-config/route-fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route_group":"webhook-highfanout","enable":false}'
```

jon.oncall: I'll own pager watch during the window. Mika will own dashboards and verify quality regressions with a small eval set. Support lead please standby for any customer noise.

support-lead: Standing by 02:00-03:30 UTC. I'll prepare a short support note explaining: "fallback enabled to preserve latency; quality impact minimal for these routes; contact support if you see issues."

rachel.sre: Scheduled maintenance (policy and sharding tune) next Tue 03:00-04:00 UTC to increase hotset caps and change eviction throttle logic. High level plan: canary per-pool, 5% -> 30% -> region. We'll also add a new metric: kvcache-hotset-occupancy and a soft-threshold alert to catch hotspots early.

bench-bot: Suggested preflight: run a targeted loadgen against the affected prefixes simulating the production fanout distribution for 15m to validate new caps. Command:
```
loadgen run --job cache-recap-2015556789 --prefixes "/webhook-cache/,/session/ctx/" --qps 1500 --duration 900
```

ops-bot: Abort criteria for Tue maintenance: sustained P95 delta >400ms for 10m, cache-eviction-rate spike >2x baseline for 5m, or error-rate >0.5% absolute. If abort -> revert cap changes, disable new eviction throttle, and open incident.

mika.prod: For the scheduled maintenance, can we include a small 'quiet window' where app teams can opt-out? Some teams have experiments that can't tolerate even minor quality changes.

rachel.sre: Yes. We'll accept opt-outs until Mon 23:59 UTC. We'll skip any route groups marked with metadata opt-out. Also will publish a maintenance notice in the console.

jon.oncall: Who are owners?

rachel.sre: Jon runs the emergency rollout tonight. Mika runs the Tue maintenance. I'll lead postmortem and policy change PR. Bench-bot will run perf tests and post summaries. Deploy-bot will post job status updates here during actions.

support-lead: I'll draft a FAQ blurb for customers and stage it in the support playbook.

rachel.sre: Final notes: we'll add a short eval harness to the canary to compare compact-model outputs for the affected routes; Mika please add 20 sample prompts for quick quality checks. I'll post the runbook link and exact job ids 30m before each window. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
